newsitem.title: USA: Moderate earthquake hits Seattle area, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake hits Seattle area, no injuries.

text.p: A moderate earthquake measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale shook the Puget Sound area on Monday but there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
According to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), the temblor hit at 12:13 p.m. PDT (1913 GMT) and was centred 15 miles (24 km) west of Seattle.
One aftershock measuring 2.8 was recorded about 15 minutes later.
Monday's quake was the most serious in the region since May 2, 1996, when one measuring 5.5 struck northeast of Seattle.
Monday's temblor occurred in the Seattle Fault Zone, which runs westward from Seattle across Puget Sound to Bremerton. The fault zone has been the subject of research by the USGS over the past year.
